intervention_label: High-resolution HLA typing (A*02:01 / A*24:02) + HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor
expected_benefit: Resolves the allele-level HLA-A*02:01 (and A*24:02) status and the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch that gate every HLA-restricted lever the case was submitted to surface.
key_risks: None from the assay itself (blood draw or retrieval of the archived 2020 typing record)
Time cost: HLA typing 3-7 days (STAT available); HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is a 1-3 week specialized send-out needing a fresh sibling-donor sample and donor consent
preference_alignment: matches the stated priority (de-risk the HLA-restricted immunotherapy pathway): YES; non-toxic and gates the referral's own question.
guideline_status: Not a therapy; enables NCCN AML v3.2026 category-2A clinical-trial enrollment for the HLA-restricted programs.
rationale_summary: Every HLA-restricted lever (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1-C4, PRAME-directed cells) is presented on HLA-A*02:01, whose allele-level status is not in the records on hand, and HLA-identical siblings can still differ at HA-1/HA-2, so the mismatch must be genotyped in both patient and donor. All five personas treated this as the non-toxic first action that gates everything downstream. A*24:02 is pulled in parallel to keep the WT1-siTCR fallback alive if A*02:01 is negative. Retrieve the ~2020 transplant typing before re-drawing. This is the rank-1 shared workup that decides whether the ranking's biomarker-conditional recs apply at all.
open_questions: Whether the ~2020 allele-level typing report can be confirmed without a re-draw
Whether the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch runs in the required recipient-positive / donor-negative direction
TP53 status and Y220C variant are a separate, parallel gate carried as open questions on the p53-directed rows
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic gate, not a therapy: opens or closes the entire HLA-restricted axis; a negative allele call forecloses the rank-3 rec outright rather than downgrading it.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic test on blood / archival record)
overall: The master switch for this run: every HLA-restricted option is stranded until allele-level typing and HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and donor return.

intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning + second allo-HCT
expected_benefit: SIERRA durable CR (>=180d) 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) vs 0% on conventional care, p<0.0001; EFS HR 0.23 (95% CI 0.15-0.34); carries an 85%-blast marrow into a second transplant.
key_risks: Grade 3+ treatment-related AEs 59.7% vs 59.2% conventional care (no incremental conditioning burden), plus standard cytopenias/infection/mucositis
Second-transplant treatment-related mortality uncharacterized by SIERRA
No cardiac/renal/hepatic labs on file — conditioning not deliverable until fitness clears
preference_alignment: matches curative intent and no-modality-ruled-out: YES; efficacy-leaning 0.75 weight: YES; trial route: YES (though timing gap).
guideline_status: ELN 2022 and NCCN AML v3.2026 keep second allo-HCT + trial enrollment in play; Iomab-B enters via the category-2A clinical-trial route, no drug-level category.
rationale_summary: SIERRA is the one randomized phase 3 in the dossier that fits the actual problem — getting active disease to a transplant — and all five personas endorsed it. Two limits are load-bearing: the endpoint is a surrogate (ITT OS flat at HR 0.99, diluted by 52% crossover) and SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so prior-HCT eligibility is indirect. As conditioning it adds essentially no incremental grade 3+ toxicity. It is the platform on which the rank-3 HA-1 TCR-T consolidation would be delivered. Fitness and organ-function workup must precede it.
open_questions: Prior-HCT eligibility for CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning (SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients)
When the go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 opens and whether it accepts a second transplant
Cardiac/renal/hepatic fitness for a second conditioning
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate: the only randomized signal in the dossier (SIERRA dCR 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001), read indirectly onto a prior-HCT relapse it did not enroll.
toxicity_burden: High (grade 3+ TRAEs 59.7%, at parity with conventional care — conditioning cytopenias, infection, mucositis; second-transplant TRM uncharacterized)

counter_productive_moa.description: Radioconjugate marrow injury could compromise engraftment if the HCT2 platform is not secured; no mechanism objection raised.

overall: The curative backbone all five personas endorsed — the randomized way to carry active disease into a second transplant, gated on a fitness workup that has not yet been done.

intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / BSB-1001)
expected_benefit: Krakow 2024: CR achieved or maintained in 4/9 post-allo-HCT relapses, one past two years; lineage-restricted graft-versus-leukemia with curative intent.
key_risks: Lymphodepletion-driven grade 3-4 neutropenia and grade 3-5 infection (Legionella, S. aureus pneumonia)
Two mild grade 1-2 acute GVHD (attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal, not the TCR-T)
TCR-T kinetics may lag an 85%-blast marrow; needs cytoreduction + HCT2 platform first
preference_alignment: matches the stated HLA-restricted-immunotherapy priority: YES; prefers trials (3 recruiting slots): YES; efficacy-leaning weight not traded against tolerability (0 CRS / 0 ICANS): YES.
guideline_status: NCCN AML v3.2026 category-2A clinical-trial-enrollment route; no drug-level category; ELN 2022 gives no sequencing consensus for post-HCT relapse.
rationale_summary: This is the exact lever the referral was submitted to surface, and four personas ranked it; only the conservative left it off, explicitly declining to veto and calling the clean safety read the opposite of their worry. The critic's evidence-tier caution — n=9 feasibility, no comparator, 4/9 CR inseparable from lymphodepletion — is not biomarker-contingent and persists in the positive branch. The whole rec is gated on HLA-A*02:01 confirmation plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch; a negative typing result forecloses it rather than downgrading it. It is delivered as post-HCT2 consolidation, not a standalone. Ranked below the unanimously endorsed transplant platform that makes it deliverable.
open_questions: HLA-A*02:01 allele status and the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch direction (both pending — the gating workup)
If A*02:01-negative but A*24:02-positive, the A*24:02 WT1-siTCR is the only within-scope fallback (no open route today)
Autologous/donor T-cell fitness and manufacturing lead-time alignment with the HCT2 timeline
likelihood_of_effect: Assuming A*02:01 + HA-1 mismatch confirm: uncertain but curative-intent — 4/9 CR in Krakow 2024 (n=9 feasibility, no comparator). Negative typing forecloses it.
toxicity_burden: Low (no CRS, no ICANS, no DLTs across n=9; lymphodepletion neutropenia and grade 3-5 infection; mild grade 1-2 GVHD)

counter_productive_moa.description: TCR-T kinetics may lag an 85%-blast marrow and antigen-loss escape is possible; lineage-restricted killing limits off-target collateral.

overall: The only lever that answers the referral's own question — a clean-safety, curative-intent graft-versus-leukemia consolidation, live only if the pending typing confirms and delivered after HCT2.
scenario_label: If HLA-A*02:01 confirmed (allele-level) with the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch present

expected_benefit: First-line CR/clinical CR 72% (21/29) at 12 ug/kg in BPDCN (cross-tumor); preclinically kills CD123+ AML/MDS blasts including low-density cells (bridge-to-transplant framing).
key_risks: Capillary leak syndrome 19% (boxed warning) with one death per dose subgroup
Hepatic transaminase elevation (ALT 64%, AST 60%) and hypoalbuminemia 55%
No baseline albumin/cardiac/hepatic workup on file
preference_alignment: matches CD123 as a user-named handle and prefers-trials (NCT06561152): PARTIAL; off-label cross-tumor use tempers alignment.
guideline_status: FDA-approved in BPDCN only; no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing — AML use is off-label cross-tumor read-across.
rationale_summary: The conservative ranked tagraxofusp over pivekimab and flotetuzumab specifically for its worked-out capillary-leak management algorithm and years of post-marketing safety — the one CD123 option with an FDA label. But the 72% CR is a first-line BPDCN number, and the critic and concensusite filed qualified cautions that it does not transfer to an 85%-blast AML marrow and carries no AML guideline standing. It stays in the Experimental table because it is approved only in BPDCN and off-label/investigational for this AML patient, and it is carried with caveats: presenting off-label cross-tumor efficacy as standard care would misstate its footing. CD123 is confirmed present but the quantitative density that predicts benefit is pending.
open_questions: Quantitative CD123 antigen density (pending) that predicts benefit
Baseline albumin and cardiac/hepatic reserve before capillary-leak-prone therapy
Whether cross-tumor BPDCN efficacy transfers to high-burden AML at all
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-uncertain for AML: headline 72% CR is first-line BPDCN cross-tumor (Pemmaraju 2019); no AML efficacy data and CD123 density still pending.
toxicity_burden: High (capillary leak syndrome with treatment-related deaths, transaminitis ALT 64% / AST 60%, hypoalbuminemia 55%)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanistic antagonism; the efficacy risk is cross-tumor non-transfer from BPDCN, and on-target killing of normal CD34+CD123+ progenitors adds myelosuppression.

overall: The only labeled CD123 agent with a real safety algorithm, but its headline efficacy is BPDCN cross-tumor and its capillary-leak deaths demand organ-function labs first.

expected_benefit: Lulla 2021: 1 CR + 1 PR of 8 in the active-disease cohort; median leukemia-free and overall survival not reached at 1.9y; hits WT1 and PRAME without a single-HLA gate.
key_risks: No grade >2 acute GVHD and no extensive chronic GVHD across n=25 (favorable safety)
Modest published activity in active disease (2/8)
WT1 and PRAME expression on the blasts not yet confirmed
preference_alignment: matches curative intent, prefers-trials (recruiting, 2 US sites), and keeps an immunotherapy route open if A*02:01 is negative: YES.
guideline_status: Investigational; NCCN AML v3.2026 category-2A clinical-trial-enrollment route; no drug-level category.
rationale_summary: The advocate flagged this as a live fallback rather than ranking it: a multi-antigen donor T-cell product that targets WT1 and PRAME (both stated handles) without depending on the single HLA-A*02:01 gate, so it keeps an immunotherapy route open if the master switch types negative. It has published clinical precedent (responses in active disease) and a clean GVHD safety profile, and it is recruiting in the post-transplant setting the patient is heading toward. No board persona ranked it, so it carries no endorsement score, but it is enrollable and feature-targeting, so it is surfaced as a considered-with-caveats option. WT1/PRAME expression should be confirmed first, and the product would be generated from the existing sibling donor.
open_questions: WT1 and PRAME expression on the blasts (drives eligibility)
Adult enrollment and post-HCT timing at the two US sites
Whether a donor-derived product can be generated from the sibling donor
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-modest: 2/8 objective responses in active disease (Lulla 2021); hits WT1/PRAME without a single-HLA gate, but WT1/PRAME expression unconfirmed.
toxicity_burden: Low (no grade >2 acute GVHD, no extensive chronic GVHD across n=25)

counter_productive_moa.description: Multi-antigen targeting limits single-antigen escape; no mechanism that blunts the goal.

overall: A multi-antigen donor T-cell hedge that sidesteps the A*02:01 gate and is enrollable post-transplant — but published activity is modest and WT1/PRAME expression is still to confirm.

expected_benefit: Single-agent ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% at the RP2D in R/R AML — own-disease data, unlike the other CD123 options.
key_risks: Veno-occlusive disease at higher doses (dose-limiting, reversible) and one treatment-related death across the study
RP2D grade 3+ febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion reactions 7%, anaemia 7%
No hepatic/albumin baselines on file, and a second transplant is planned
preference_alignment: matches CD123 handle, prefers-trials, and efficacy-leaning debulking rationale: YES on preference axes — but overridden by the toxicity veto given the planned HCT2.
guideline_status: FDA-approved (Decnupaz) for BPDCN only, May 2026; off-label/investigational for AML; AML trials closed to enrollment.
rationale_summary: The risktaker and advocate ranked pivekimab as a CD123-directed debulking bridge with real R/R AML numbers, but the conservative issued a veto on toxicity grounds: a documented veno-occlusive-disease signal ahead of a second transplant in a patient with no hepatic or albumin labs on file. The veto is conditional and explicitly liftable — it reinstates the moment baseline bilirubin, transaminases and a hepatic read clear it — but that condition is unmet, so the veto stands and the row is preserved as not_recommended rather than dropped. This is a mechanism-level risk, not just a patient AE: VOD could compromise the very transplant the debulking is meant to enable. Quantitative CD123 density is still pending.
open_questions: Baseline bilirubin, transaminases and a hepatic read (the veto's stated lifting condition)
Quantitative CD123 antigen density (tracks ADC potency in the preclinical work)
Whether any enrolling AML cohort or expanded-access route reopens
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate as debulking: own R/R AML data (ORR 21%, 95% CI 8-40; cCR 17%), but single-agent depth is modest against an 85%-blast marrow.
toxicity_burden: High (veno-occlusive disease at higher doses, one treatment-related death; RP2D febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion reactions 7%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Veno-occlusive disease from the ADC ahead of HCT2 could sink the very transplant the debulking is meant to enable.

overall: The CD123 ADC with the best own-disease data, held under a live, conditional VOD veto — it reinstates as a debulking bridge the moment hepatic and albumin baselines clear it.

expected_benefit: Off-the-shelf subcutaneous T-cell engager against CG1 on HLA-A*02:01; no cell-manufacturing lead time; prior allo-HCT allowed after 60 days.
key_risks: First-in-human phase 1 with no efficacy readout yet
T-cell-engager cytokine-release risk against a high blast burden
HLA-A*02:01 typing still pending; CG1 is not one of the named antigen handles
preference_alignment: matches prefers-trials and the HLA-A*02:01 axis, with a no-lead-time advantage in a fast-moving relapse: PARTIAL (no efficacy data).
guideline_status: Investigational, first-in-human; NCCN AML v3.2026 category-2A trial-enrollment route only.
rationale_summary: CBX-250 sits on the same HLA-A*02:01 master switch as the HA-1/HA-2 and WT1 levers but, as an off-the-shelf engager, skips the cell-manufacturing wait that matters in an 85%-blast relapse, and it is recruiting at 11 US sites. It has no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy — a first-in-human phase 1 with no efficacy readout — so it is surfaced as thin_evidence rather than ranked as a live top-tier choice, and it targets CG1 rather than a user-named antigen. The board did not rank it; the advocate noted it as a fallback for its timeline advantage. Live and enrollable, but unproven.
open_questions: HLA-A*02:01 status (the single gating biomarker for this engager)
Whether the 60-day post-transplant window is met and CRS can be managed at high blast burden
No efficacy data exists yet to weigh against the faster timeline
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: first-in-human phase 1, no efficacy readout; the argument is the off-the-shelf no-lead-time timeline, not a proven number.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (T-cell-engager cytokine-release risk against high blast burden; no reported grade profile yet)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen escape or T-cell exhaustion possible; no board mechanism objection, and no efficacy data to weigh either way.

overall: An off-the-shelf A*02:01 engager with a real no-lead-time advantage and 11 recruiting US sites, but zero efficacy data — enrollable yet unproven, gated on the same allele call.

expected_benefit: Preclinically restores wild-type p53 conformation in TP53-Y220C AML and prolongs xenograft survival — but only when combined with venetoclax; no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy yet.
key_risks: No published clinical efficacy or toxicity to extract (myeloid and solid-tumor trials report only abstracts)
Single-agent rezatapopt was largely cytostatic in AML; the survival signal needed venetoclax, which this disease already progressed through
Double-gated: requires confirming TP53 aberrant AND specifically Y220C
preference_alignment: matches the user-named TP53 handle and prefers-trials (NCT06616636): PARTIAL — cannot carry a live rank without the Y220C confirmation and clinical data.
guideline_status: Investigational; no approval, no guideline listing; myeloid trial single-site (MD Anderson).
rationale_summary: Rezatapopt is the Y220C-selective handle the profile names, and every persona left it off their ranked picks for the same reason: it has no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy (logged considered_excluded upstream) and is double-gated on confirming TP53 aberration and specifically the Y220C variant. The risktaker noted it would jump up fast if Y220C confirms, given the strong Carter 2025 AML preclinical signal, but that signal needed venetoclax to produce killing and this disease has already progressed through FLAG-IDA/venetoclax. Surfaced as thin_evidence, not ranked. TP53 is the second non-confirmed biomarker (capped out of the branched output); its resolution is carried as an open question here rather than a parallel branch.
open_questions: Resolve TP53 status without collapsing the 2019-mutant vs 2026-negative discrepancy (retrieve 2019 variant + VAF, add p53 IHC and 17p FISH, CNV-capable NGS)
Whether the specific variant is Y220C (the therapy handle) vs a non-Y220C aberration (which removes the option)
Expected depth given prior venetoclax progression
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown clinically: strong Y220C AML preclinical signal (Carter 2025) but no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy, and killing required venetoclax the disease has progressed through.
toxicity_burden: Low (none extractable — no published clinical toxicity yet)

counter_productive_moa.description: Single-agent reactivation is largely cytostatic without BCL-2 inhibition; prior venetoclax progression may blunt the combination that makes it work.

overall: The Y220C-selective TP53 handle that enters contention only if the variant confirms — double-gated on TP53 status and Y220C, with no clinical efficacy data yet to rank on.

key_risks: No published clinical results yet for the commercial product (efficacy read carried by the Bleakley platform)
Same eligibility gate as rank 3: A*02:01 + recipient HA-1(H)+/donor HA-1- mismatch, both pending

Eligibility and board signal are identical to the ranked approach. Refer to rank 3 for the full evidence and dissent picture.

overall: The commercial HA-1 arm of the ranked approach, recruiting at 21 US sites — same gate, same board signal, consolidated under rank 3.

The critic dissented that the TP53 signal is post-hoc correlative rather than an effect estimate, and the concensusite dissented on guideline grounds (no listing, closed trial); both objections stand regardless of TP53 status. Whether an open CD123xCD3 construct can carry the mechanism instead

rationale_summary: The advocate ranked this to keep the immunotherapy door open if A*02:01 types negative: it is A*24:02-restricted, so an A*02:01-negative but A*24:02-positive patient still has a route rather than a dead end. The critic and concensusite filed qualified notes that the evidence (Tawara 2017, n=8, transient responses) is route-preservation rather than an efficacy signal. But the published work is a small completed Japanese academic cohort with no open AML/MDS successor, so it is surfaced as unavailable today. It is the reason both HLA alleles must be pulled in parallel. This is the negative-branch fallback the cross-cutting caveat names; the contract emits no parallel negative-branch ranking.

It is the replication-failure exhibit the critic named — strong single-arm ORR, then a negative randomized trial. Surfaced as unavailable. If a p53-reactivation strategy is pursued, the Y220C-selective rezatapopt (rank 8) is the better-supported track, contingent on confirming Y220C.
